name: Cursor
knownFor: An AI-first code editor. Public pricing is now the X Subscription ladder, shared with Grok, with third-party models billed separately on higher plans.
popCaption: Editorial estimate · checked Nov 2026. Cursor is the most widely discussed dedicated AI editor in this set; there is no public seat-count table in this research pass.
pro: A dedicated coding product with a published price ladder
con: Plus is Grok-only; third-party model spend is extra on Premium and above
costCaption: Official cursor.com/pricing (checked Nov 2026), matching x.ai/pricing: Free; Plus $8/month (Grok models only); Premium $30/month (labeled most popular; third-party models at API list price); Super $100/month; Ultra $200/month. Teams start at $30+/user/month. Rated on Premium, the plan the page marks as most popular for serious use.

name: GitHub Copilot
knownFor: The default in-editor assistant for many GitHub users, available as an extension, in github.com, and as a CLI.
popCaption: Editorial estimate · checked Nov 2026. Copilot’s distribution inside GitHub and VS Code is the reason for the score; no public seat-count was found this session.
learn: Completion and chat inside an existing editor
pro: Clear official individual price and huge distribution through GitHub and VS Code
con: Popularity is editorial (no public seat-count); higher plans add a lot of cost
costCaption: Official GitHub Docs, “Plans for GitHub Copilot” (docs.github.com, checked Nov 2026): Copilot Pro $10/month (free for some users); Copilot Pro+ $39/month; Copilot Max $100/month; Copilot Business $19/user/month; Copilot Enterprise $39/user/month. Rated on Copilot Pro, the typical individual paid plan.

name: Claude Code
knownFor: Anthropic’s coding agent (terminal, IDE, and related surfaces), included with paid Claude plans rather than sold as a separate seat.
popCaption: Editorial estimate, tied to Claude’s rising web traffic (11.5% of seven-assistant website visits in October 2026, Similarweb — that is not a Claude Code-specific figure) · checked Nov 2026
learn: An agent in the terminal or IDE
pro: Bundled with a clearly priced Claude plan
con: Usage is shared with the rest of the Claude plan; heavy coding can hit limits
costCaption: Included with Claude paid plans. Official claude.com/pricing (checked Nov 2026) lists Claude Pro at $20/month ($17/month billed annually) and includes Claude Code. Max is $100/month and Ultra is $200/month. Rated on Pro. API coding use is separate except for credits on higher plans.

name: OpenAI Codex
knownFor: OpenAI’s coding agent, available in ChatGPT, a CLI, IDE extensions, and related Cloud/work surfaces.
popCaption: Editorial estimate, with distribution through ChatGPT (55.7% of seven-assistant website visits in October 2026, Similarweb — not a Codex-specific figure) · checked Nov 2026
learn: A coding agent next to ChatGPT
pro: Bundled with the most-visited assistant in the Similarweb set
con: Limits and surfaces vary by plan; this is not only an in-editor extension
costCaption: Codex access is described on ChatGPT plans. Rated on ChatGPT Plus at $20/month (OpenAI Help, checked Nov 2026). chatgpt.com/pricing and OpenAI Help also describe expanded Codex usage on Plus and Pro. API-key usage is billed separately at API rates.

name: Windsurf
knownFor: An AI-first editor (the Windsurf / Codeium line) with a straightforward individual Pro plan.
con: Smaller public footprint than Cursor or GitHub Copilot in this research pass
costCaption: Official windsurf.com/pricing (checked Nov 2026): Free; Pro $20/month (labeled popular); Max $200/month. Teams are $80/month for the team plan plus $40/month per full dev seat. Rated on Pro.

name: Gemini Code Assist
knownFor: Google’s coding assistant, available in IDEs, Android Studio, and Google’s AI developer tools, including higher usage on paid Google AI plans.
popCaption: Editorial estimate, with distribution through Google’s developer tools and AI plans · checked Nov 2026
learn: Completion and agents in a Google toolchain
pro: Sits next to Android Studio, Cloud, and Gemini
con: The exact seat can be a Google AI plan or a Cloud/Workspace SKU, depending on the surface
costCaption: Tied to Google AI and Google Cloud / developer plans. Official one.google.com/about/google-ai-plans (checked Nov 2026) describes AI-assisted coding features and Cloud credits on Google AI paid plans. Rated on Google AI Pro at $19.99/month as a typical individual paid path. Some features also sit on Cloud or Workspace plans — confirm on Google’s current Code Assist page.

name: Amazon Q Developer
knownFor: AWS’s coding assistant, aimed at people already building on Amazon Web Services.
pro: Natural fit if the team is already on AWS
con: Official individual price was not captured this session
costCaption: Amazon Q Developer is sold as a free tier plus a paid individual or Professional plan on AWS. This session did not capture a current official individual monthly figure from the AWS pricing page. Editorial estimate $$ for a typical individual paid plan. Confirm current prices on aws.amazon.com/q/developer/pricing.

name: Tabnine
knownFor: A long-running completion assistant, including options aimed at privacy-conscious and enterprise teams.
pro: A dedicated coding product older than the current editor wave
con: Official price was not captured this session
costCaption: Tabnine sells individual and team plans. This session did not capture a current official individual monthly figure. Editorial estimate $$ for a typical individual plan. Confirm current prices on tabnine.com/pricing.

name: JetBrains AI
knownFor: The AI assistant built into JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ, PyCharm, and others), sold as a JetBrains AI subscription or as part of a JetBrains plan.
popCaption: Editorial estimate, based on JetBrains’ large existing IDE user base rather than a public AI-seat count · checked Nov 2026
learn: People who already live in IntelliJ or PyCharm
pro: Native to a very widely used IDE family
con: Official AI-add-on price was not captured this session
costCaption: JetBrains AI is sold as an add-on or as part of a JetBrains subscription. This session did not capture a current official individual monthly figure. Editorial estimate $$ for a typical individual AI add-on. Confirm current prices on jetbrains.com.

name: Cline
knownFor: An open-source coding agent (VS Code and similar), often used with your own model API keys.
popCaption: 71,633 GitHub stars on cline/cline (GitHub API, checked Nov 14, 2026). Stars measure interest, not paid seats.
learn: An open agent in VS Code
con: Your real cost is the model API, which varies widely
costCaption: The Cline project is free and open source. You pay separately for whatever model API you connect. Rated Free for the tool itself; model spend is usage-based and not invented here.

name: Aider
knownFor: An open-source, terminal-based coding agent that edits a local repo with a connected model.
popCaption: 50,118 GitHub stars on Aider-AI/aider (GitHub API, checked Nov 14, 2026). Stars measure interest, not paid seats.
learn: A terminal agent over a git repo
con: Your real cost is the model API, which varies widely
costCaption: Aider is free and open source. You pay separately for the model API you connect. Rated Free for the tool itself; model spend is usage-based and not invented here.

name: Continue
knownFor: An open-source IDE extension that can connect to many local or hosted models.
popCaption: 36,481 GitHub stars on continuedev/continue (GitHub API, checked Nov 14, 2026). Stars measure interest, not paid seats.
con: The assistant is only as good as the model you attach
costCaption: The Continue extension is free and open source. You pay separately for whatever model you connect, or you can use a local model. Rated Free for the tool itself.
